implementation_notes: Swift's concurrency model provides the cancellation half natively - child tasks are cancelled with their parent, Task.isCancelled is sticky and checked cooperatively, and withTaskCancellationHandler adapts cancellation to a resource - but the standard library does not yet ship a deadline operator. SE-0526 (withDeadline, accepted) will take an absolute instant and cancel the operation when it passes, compositing multiple operations under one deadline with nesting taking the minimum, which is exactly propagation-friendly; until it lands the budget must be raced by hand with a task group and Task.sleep, or supplied by a package. Carry the deadline as a ContinuousClock.Instant (monotonic) and check Task.isCancelled at each stage.
idiom_name: structured task cancellation + hand-rolled deadline race (withDeadline pending)
pitfalls: Cancellation is cooperative: a CPU loop or blocking C call never observes it, and withTaskCancellationHandler only adapts the resource - the code must still check Task.isCancelled or hit a cancelling await.
A task group waits for all of its children on exit, so a child that ignores cancellation keeps the group (and the request) alive past the deadline.
The instance Task.isCancelled ignores active cancellation shields while the static property respects them - choosing the wrong one reports cancellation inside code that was meant to be shielded.

There is no stdlib deadline operator yet, so the sleep-race must cancel the group and release resources itself when the deadline wins; SE-0526 withDeadline (accepted) will replace this hand-rolled form.
